ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows three adjacent squares resting on the same horizontal baseline. The largest square is labeled A and has bottom side JK. To its right is a smaller square labeled B with bottom side KL. To the right of B is the smallest square labeled C with bottom side LM. The bottom points are labeled in order J, K, L, M. The squares share vertical sides internally, so only the outside outline counts for the perimeter. Reasoning: Let LM = x. Since KL = 2LM, KL = 2x. Since JK = 2KL, JK = 4x. Thus the side lengths of squares A, B, and C are 4x, 2x, and x respectively. Trace the outside boundary: bottom JM = 4x + 2x + x = 7x; right side of C = x; top of C = x; exposed right side of B above C = 2x - x = x; top of B = 2x; exposed right side of A above B = 4x - 2x = 2x; top of A = 4x; left side of A = 4x. Therefore the perimeter is 7x + x + x + x + 2x + 2x + 4x + 4x = 22x. Given perimeter 66, 22x = 66, so x = 3. The total area is the sum of the three square areas: (4x)^2 + (2x)^2 + x^2 = 16x^2 + 4x^2 + x^2 = 21x^2. With x = 3, area = 21 · 9 = 189.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a union of three squares arranged side by side, where square A shares a vertical edge segment with square B, and square B shares a vertical edge segment with square C. Let LM = x, so the side lengths of C, B, and A are x, 2x, and 4x respectively. Instead of tracing the outside, start with the sum of the perimeters of the three separate squares: 4x + 8x + 16x = 28x. The internal shared edges are not part of the outside perimeter: A and B share an edge of length 2x, and B and C share an edge of length x. These shared edges were counted twice in the separate perimeters, so subtract 2(2x + x) = 6x. Therefore the combined perimeter is 28x - 6x = 22x. Since 22x = 66, x = 3. The total area is x^2 + (2x)^2 + (4x)^2 = 21x^2 = 189.
